title: rectoverso.json
description: A deck's description of itself, at the root of its repository: the single source of truth for its identity, its words, its languages, its credits and its options. docs/contract.md explains every field. A deck may keep keys of its own beside these; RectoVerso leaves them aside.

id.description: The deck's id, stable for good: its repository's name.

version.description: This edition: major.minor.patch, with -rc.<n> for a release candidate.

releaseTag.description: The Git tag of this edition: "v" and the version.

guidPrefix.description: What every note's GUID starts with, before the language: lowercase words and digits, hyphens between them.

identityBase.description: The base of the Anki ids the deck gives its note types and decks.

contentModifiedAt.description: When the content last changed (ISO 8601). It moves forward with every content change, never into the future: Anki updates a note only when it is newer.

publication.description: Where the deck is published, and whether its owner has approved this edition.

remote.description: The repository's URL; its last part is the deck's id.

release.description: This edition's release page: the remote, then /releases/tag/ and the release tag.

approved.description: Whether this edition is approved for publication. Only an approved deck enters a gallery.

visibility.description: "private" for a Pro-only deck, "public" for every other.

title.description: The deck's plain title, in every language it ships.

subject.description: What the deck is about, in a word or two, in every language it ships.

headline.description: One line that says what the learner gets, in every language it ships.

description.description: A short description, in every language it ships.

whatsNew.description: This edition's notes, in one or more of the languages it ships.

playLabel.description: The word on the questions' sound button, in one or more of the languages it ships. Without one, the button says Play.

study.description: The study options the deck comes into the library with, for a course whose new cards build on each other. An option left out keeps the app's default.

newCards.description: New cards at random, or in the order the deck was written.

newPosition.description: New cards after the reviews, before them, or mixed in.

categories.description: One or more of the gallery's categories, each once. The first places the deck in the gallery's sections.

cards.description: How many cards each language's package makes.

pictures.description: How many pictures the deck credits: the length of imageCredits.

license.description: The deck's own license: an open one (CC0-1.0, CC-BY-4.0, CC-BY-SA-4.0, MIT, Apache-2.0, Public domain), or, for a Pro-only deck, its own terms as a LicenseRef- identifier.

sources.description: Where the content comes from: at least one source.

license.description: An open license: never non-commercial (NC) or no-derivatives (ND).

file.description: The picture's file name, with no folder.

original.description: For a deck whose build renders its pictures: the file in the repository this picture is rendered from.

proOnly.description: Whether the deck is offered only with RectoVerso Pro.

renderedPictures.description: Whether the deck's build renders its pictures, which then stay out of Git: each credit names its original instead.

sourceFiles.description: The paths, inside the repository, the deck builds from: "pictures" and "sounds" are the folders the cards' media are in; other keys are the deck's own.

languages.description: Each language the deck ships, by its code: a package of its own, with ids of its own.

id.description: This language's package id, stable for good.

title.description: The deck's title in this language: the same as title's.

cards.description: How many cards this language's package makes: the same as cards.

sample.description: The one card the gallery opens as a sample question: a note's GUID, or "<GUID>/<n>" for the nth card of a note that makes several.

file.description: The package's file name on the release.

covers.description: The gallery's pictures of the deck, per language: one or more for light mode and one or more for dark mode, in the order shown.
